prompt: I run a Shopify store and I'm losing sales every time something sells out — shoppers see "Sold out" and leave without telling me they were interested. I want a "Notify me when back in stock" app so any shopper can leave their email on a sold-out item and hear from me the moment it's available again, and I can see in the admin which products people are waiting on so I know what to restock. Shoppers should sign up at the variant level when a product has multiple variants like sizes or colors (they pick the exact one and only get notified about that one), or at the product level when there's nothing meaningful to choose between — default to whichever fits. The widget sits on the product page right under the sold-out button, takes an email, confirms inline, and never appears on items already in stock. When something is back, every shopper waiting should be emailed in the order they signed up; if only a few units come back and many are waiting, notify the front of the queue and keep the rest for the next restock, and each shopper hears about a given item once per restock so no duplicate blasts if stock briefly dips. In the admin I want a dashboard ranking products by waitlist size, a drill-in to see individual subscribers and export them as CSV, an editor for the email subject and body (with product name, item details, and a one-click unsubscribe link), and quiet hours so nothing sends late at night. Every email needs a working unsubscribe that clears the shopper from all their waitlists; deleted products clear their waitlist cleanly; duplicate signups for the same item from the same email are a no-op; the same email across many products is fine. The number I care about most is "lost demand recovered" — how many signed up, how many got notified, and how many of those actually bought that item within a week.

intent.desiredOutcome: Recover lost sales by capturing shopper demand for sold-out items, notifying them reliably when stock returns, and measuring how many sales result.
intent.cronHint: Every 30 minutes (or merchant-configurable schedule) during quiet hours
intent.qualityBrief: A polished back-in-stock app handles duplicate webhook delivery (idempotent signup and restock sends), guest checkout (no customer ID, email alone is the key), partial restocks (queue management and per-restock-per-shopper deduplication), deleted/unpublished products (safe cascade of waitlist), and variant-level subscriptions correctly (same product, different variants = separate queues). UX must show empty states gracefully, give instant inline confirmation to the shopper, and let the merchant export CSV reliably. The metrics page must track signup → send → purchase attribution within the 7-day window, account for bounced emails and unsubscribes in the send count, and survive duplicate restock events without double-crediting. Quiet hours must be timezone-aware and merchant-configurable. The email template must render product images, variant-specific details (size, color label), and a one-click unsubscribe that works without re-entering the email.

plan.dataFlow: A shopper on a sold-out product page submits their email through the storefront widget, which records a waitlist subscription for the exact item (variant-level when the product has meaningful options, product-level otherwise) and confirms inline; duplicate submissions for the same item and email are a no-op. When an item's stock returns, the inventory-change event resolves the affected item, and if it is now available the system claims the front of that item's waitlist queue in signup order, opens a notification batch keyed to this restock, and emails each claimed shopper once (respecting quiet hours and the merchant's template), leaving any overflow shoppers queued for the next restock. Each email carries a one-click unsubscribe link that clears the shopper from all their waitlists. When an order is paid, the system attributes purchases back to recently-notified subscribers within a seven-day window to compute lost-demand-recovered. The merchant browses a waitlist-ranked dashboard, drills into subscribers, exports CSV, edits the email template, and configures quiet hours and the restock-scan schedule in the admin; deleted products cascade their waitlists away cleanly.

triggers.idempotency: a restock for an item is processed once per restock occurrence; a notification batch keyed to the item and restock occurrence prevents the same shopper being emailed twice if stock briefly dips and recovers within the same batch window

attribution for the same order is recorded once; duplicate order-paid deliveries do not double-credit a purchase

triggers.cadence: every 30 minutes, merchant-configurable, only dispatching during allowed hours
triggers.jobPurpose: Dispatch pending back-in-stock notifications that were deferred because they fell within quiet hours, in signup order.
triggers.perTickWork: Select notification records that are due (their item is available and the current time is outside the merchant's quiet hours), send each email via the template, and mark them sent or failed.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory-change delivery for the same item within one restock window must not open a second batch or re-notify already-notified shoppers, enforced by the item-and-restock batch key and once-per-batch notification key.
Stock briefly dips to zero and recovers while a batch is still open — the same shoppers must not be emailed again because their notification already exists for that batch.
Partial restock with fewer units than waiting shoppers — notify only the front of the queue up to the available quantity and leave the rest queued for the next restock.
A restock fires during quiet hours — defer the notifications as pending and let the scheduled job dispatch them once outside the merchant's timezone-aware quiet window.
Duplicate widget signup for the same item and email is a no-op; the same email across different products or variants creates independent subscriptions.
A deleted product must cascade-remove its waitlist subscriptions and rollups so no orphaned notifications are ever sent.
Email dispatch fails or bounces — record the notification as failed or bounced and exclude it from the notified count so metrics are not inflated.
Duplicate order-paid delivery for the same order must not double-credit a purchase against the attribution window.
A shopper clicks unsubscribe before their pending notification is sent — suppress that send and clear them from all waitlists.

hld_v_findings.issue: shopifySteps declares a single op `productVariant` that `consumes: "variant external id"`, but for product-scoped subscriptions (`item_scope=product`) the widget passes a product external id — not a variant id — in `item_external_id`. `productVariant` requires a variant GID; it cannot accept a product GID. The widget state GET requestShape passes only `item_external_id` and `item_scope`, so there is no separate variant id available when scope is "product". The coding agent has no resolved op to check product-level availability, leaving the widget unable to suppress itself on in-stock product-scoped items.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a second shopifyStep using the `product` query (consuming `item_external_id` when `item_scope=product`) and note in the step sequence that the agent must branch: call `productVariant` when scope=variant and call `product` (checking whether any variant is available) when scope=product.

hld_v_findings.issue: `keyedByColumns: ["id"]` places no structural constraint on `item_external_id` for pending rows. The trigger idempotency promises "if an unprocessed restock event already exists for the item, treat the event as a no-op," but that guarantee is only as strong as the application's check-then-insert logic. Concurrent webhook deliveries (Shopify routinely delivers duplicates within milliseconds) both pass the check before either commits, inserting two pending restock events for the same item. Both are then picked up by the schedule job and every waiting subscriber is notified twice — the exact double-blast the dedup design is meant to prevent.
hld_v_findings.fix: Change `keyedByColumns` to `["item_external_id", "status"]` and add a column `status` purpose note clarifying that the uniqueness is intentionally conditional on the pending state; alternatively, add a dedicated `pending_restock_item_lock` table keyed by `["item_external_id"]` and cleared on processing, giving the DB a single-row race guard the application logic alone cannot provide.

hld_v_findings.issue: `kind: "compute"` is declared for a capability whose description reads "Claim pending restock events and allocate notifications to the front of each item's signup-ordered queue … deferring the rest." Per the spec, `compute` is "pure logic over data already in hand"; this capability reads from the DB (`restock_events`, `waitlist_subscriptions`), writes claimed status transitions (usesWorkflow), triggers email sends to external subscribers, and inserts `notifications` rows. Tagging it as `compute` tells the coding agent it may skip write-path scaffolding (DB transactions, error rollback) and the workflow claim/complete/fail wiring that `usesWorkflow: true` demands.
hld_v_findings.fix: Change `kind` to `"write"` to correctly signal that this capability mutates DB state and must be wrapped in the workflow claim/complete/fail lifecycle.

hld_v_findings.issue: `usesWorkflow: true` is set, which binds the coding agent to the platform workflow helper (atomic claim/complete/fail/sweepStale). However, this capability only records a final terminal outcome (sent / bounced / failed) on a row that was already claimed by `process-restock-queue`. Invoking the workflow helper's claim step a second time on a row that is already mid-flight is a misuse of the helper's protocol and will conflict with the open claim held by `process-restock-queue`, potentially causing a double-claim error or a lost-update on the status field.
hld_v_findings.fix: Set `usesWorkflow: false` on `record-notification-outcome` and describe it as a plain status-update write; keep `usesWorkflow: true` exclusively on `process-restock-queue`, which owns the full claim→send→complete/fail lifecycle for each notification row.
